sam_acme: Hey team — since yesterday our internal calls to api.internal.acme-pay are failing with NXDOMAIN from our app pods and we see TLS handshake errors. Started after we consolidated private hosted zones. Can you help?

julio_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Sam. Can you paste a dig +short and a curl -v from a pod where it fails? Also which VPC/account is the service endpoint in?

sam_acme: Dig and curl from a failing pod: 
```
$ dig +short api.internal.acme-pay.svc.cluster.local @169.254.20.10
;; -> (no answer)

$ curl -v https://api.internal.acme-pay/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.internal.acme-pay/health
*   Trying 10.4.8.23...
* Connected to api.internal.acme-pay (10.4.8.23) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake failed: certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) TLS handshake failure
```
We have a private ACM cert for *.internal.acme-pay issued from our Private CA, associated with the service endpoint. Hosted zone consolidation moved some private zones into the central infra account.

julio_support: Thanks. Quick triage checklist: 1) confirm private hosted zone is associated with the VPC where pods run 2) check resolver rule overrides / outbound forwarders 3) check node-local DNS cache 4) confirm cert is still valid and ACM/KMS key accessible. I'll ping eng-oncall.

ops-bot: (automated) paging ingrid_eng oncall for support thread 4260001111
ingrid_eng: Looking now. Julio — can you run a Route53 list-hosted-zones and list-vpc-association for the hosted zone name? Also any resolver rule in account?
julio_support: Running quick checks, output clipped: 
```
$ aws route53 list-hosted-zones --query 'HostedZones[?Name==`internal.acme-pay.`]'
HostedZones: [ { Id: "/hostedzone/Z123EXAMPLE", Name: "internal.acme-pay.", PrivateZone: true } ]
$ aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id /hostedzone/Z123EXAMPLE
VPCs: [ { VPCId: "vpc-0a1b2c3d", VPCRegion: "us-west-2", OwnerId: "111111111111" } ]
```
That VPCId is in our infra account (111111111111). The pods run in tenant account 222222222222 VPC vpc-0fffaaaa. So it looks like the hosted zone ended up associated to the infra account VPC only.

ingrid_eng: That would explain NXDOMAIN for tenant VPC. Two options: re-associate the private hosted zone with the tenant VPC (preferred) or create a cross-account Resolver rule + outbound endpoint. Julio, do we have a resolver rule that would forward from tenant -> infra to resolve it?
julio_support: Checking Route53Resolver rules: 
```
$ aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --region us-west-2
ResolverRules: [ { Id: "rslvr-abc", Name: "forward-infra", RuleType: "FORWARD", DomainName: "internal.acme-pay.", ResolverEndpointId: "rslvr-end-111", CreatorRequestId: "tenant-forward", OwnerId: "111111111111" } ]
```
There is a FORWARD rule in infra account. But the tenant VPC has an association? Not listed. Also tenant egress policies block outbound to the infra resolver endpoint IPs (security team had an allowlist that doesn't include those ENIs).

sam_acme: Ah — we added a strict egress allowlist last week. That could block resolver traffic to infra account resolver endpoints.

ingrid_eng: Two concurrent failures then: hosted zone not associated with tenant VPC + tenant egress blocks forwarding to infra resolver. If you want a quick fix, we can re-associate the hosted zone to the tenant VPC (requires account permission). Longer-term: re-create the private hosted zone in the tenant account or set up cross-account resolver rules with ENI IPs added to the egress allowlist.

julio_support: For certificate/TLS note: the TLS handshake error likely came from the app falling back to an IP or hitting a different backend (edge) with an unmatched cert, or from our client rejecting the cert because ACM cannot present the private cert if the endpoint is actually a different service. Once DNS resolves to the intended private IP, cert should match. But also confirm the ACM private cert's KMS CMK key policy allows the service to decrypt if it's cross-account. Run: 
```
$ aws acm describe-certificate --certificate-arn arn:aws:acm:us-west-2:111111111111:certificate/abcd-1234
```
Check Certificate.Status and DomainName. If cert uses a KMS key in infra account with restrictive policy, cross-account use may fail to present cert.

sam_acme: We did use an infra-managed private CA and the KMS key is in infra account. Our app pods are in tenant account — will that break the cert for a VPC endpoint if hosted zone is associated with tenant VPC?
ingrid_eng: If the endpoint (service) is in infra account and it serves the cert, it only needs KMS access in the infra account. If you move the hosted zone (DNS) to tenant VPC but the endpoint is still in infra, cert/KMS stays same. Cross-account KMS becomes relevant if you try to create an endpoint in the tenant account that needs to access that key. In short: DNS association problem is primary.

julio_support: Action items: 1) If you want fast resolution, ask infra (111111111111) to associate hosted zone Z123EXAMPLE with tenant VPC vpc-0fffaaaa. This can be done by route53: associate-vpc (requires owner account to call). 2) Alternatively, add the infra Resolver endpoint ENI IPs to your egress allowlist so forwarding works. 3) Verify node-local cache by restarting node-local-dns pods after zone assoc so stale NXDOMAIN clears. 4) Verify ACM cert domain and KMS policy if you still see TLS errors after DNS fix.

ops-bot: (automated) created support ticket SUP-2026-346 and linked to thread 4260001111
sam_acme: Thanks — I'll open an infra ticket to request the hosted zone association and add the ENI IPs to our allowlist as a backup. One quick question: how do we clear the NXDOMAIN cache quickly on pods?
julio_support: Exec into a pod and restart the node-local-dns DaemonSet or flush the cache. Example: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/node-local-dns
# or exec into node-local-dns container and echo "flush" to cache socket depending on implementation
```
That should clear stale NXDOMAIN entries.

ingrid_eng: I'll stay on standby after infra assoc to verify and check certificate presentation. If you want, I can also validate the route53assoc once infra confirms.

sam_acme: Ok we asked infra, they confirmed they associated the hosted zone and we added the ENI IPs to allowlist. Restarted node-local-dns. API is now resolving and TLS error is gone. Thanks all :thumbsup:

julio_support: Great to hear — marking resolved. Please let us know if anything else pops up.

aws-inspector-bot: (automated) note: hosted zone Z123EXAMPLE was associated to vpc-0fffaaaa at 2026-03-16T16:12:30Z
